summary: Read all 23 available Chinese units; checked all 14 temporal/hint items and all five people. The nine AD years are supported conventional Liao regnal-year labels. The people are attested as contemporary rulers, not credited with Later Zhou or Song calendar reforms. No local births, deaths or ages are omitted. The printed tables explicitly absent at s0024 are outside the available source and are not certified; this approval does not establish complete reproduction of the printed volume or editorial/identity readiness.

itemChecks.event: Muzong is the reigning Liao emperor in Yingli 6; the calendar action belongs to Later Zhou.
itemChecks.reason: The explicit ruler and regnal year establish contemporaneous reign attestation, not Muzong adopting the Qintian calendar. Yingli starts AD 951, so year 6 has the conventional AD 956 label. No month, exact day or life endpoint is asserted.

evidence.quote: 穆宗應歷六年，周用顯德《欽天曆》；

itemChecks.event: Muzong is the continuing Liao regnal referent in Yingli 10; Song adopts its calendar.
itemChecks.reason: The elliptical tenth year continues Yingli from the immediately preceding clause. 951 + 10 - 1 = AD 960. This is Muzong's contemporaneous reign, not a personal Song calendar reform or continuous activity from 956 through 960.

evidence.quote: 穆宗應歷六年，周用顯德《欽天曆》；
十年，宋用建隆《應天曆》。

itemChecks.event: Jingzong is explicitly named as the Liao ruler in Qianheng 4.
itemChecks.reason: Qianheng begins AD 979, giving AD 982 for year 4. Jingzong lived and reigned in that year, although the era continued under his successor: Liaoshi 009 confirms his death in its ninth month. The undated Song calendar clause must not be assigned to him as a personal action or a claim that he lived through the entire year.

evidence.quote: 景宗乾亨四年，宋用《乾元曆》。

itemChecks.event: Shengzong is the Liao regnal referent in Tonghe 19.
itemChecks.reason: The ruler is explicit; Tonghe begins AD 983, so year 19 is conventionally AD 1001. Song, not Shengzong, is the grammatical subject of using the Yitian calendar. The stored predicate is only attestation.

evidence.quote: 聖宗統和十九年，宋用《儀天曆》；

itemChecks.event: Shengzong remains the reigning Liao sovereign at Taiping 1.
itemChecks.reason: Taiping follows Shengzong's Tonghe entry, not a different polity's same-named era. Its first year begins in AD 1021. This is a regnal-year label, not a Gregorian date for Song's calendar adoption. No month or day is supplied, and the claim does not say Shengzong performed the Song action.

evidence.quote: 聖宗統和十九年，宋用《儀天曆》；
太平元年，宋用《崇天曆》。

itemChecks.event: Daozong is the Liao sovereign in Qingning 10.
itemChecks.reason: Qingning begins AD 1055, hence year 10 is AD 1064. His name qualifies the dating system; the calendar reform remains Song's action. This dated reign reference supports presence, not a birth, death or calendar commission.

evidence.quote: 道宗清寧十年，宋用《明天曆》；

itemChecks.event: Daozong is the continuing Liao ruler in Dakang 1.
itemChecks.reason: The contiguous list continues Daozong's reign context. Dakang, also written Taikang in the calendar reference, begins AD 1075. The variant spelling does not identify a different ruler or era. No life endpoint or full-reign activity is inferred.

evidence.quote: 道宗清寧十年，宋用《明天曆》；
大康元年，宋用《奉元曆》；

itemChecks.event: Daozong remains the Liao regnal referent in Da'an 7.
itemChecks.reason: Da'an begins AD 1085, so year 7 is AD 1091. The chapter's Daozong context and the calendar table distinguish this from the Xia and Jin eras with the same name. This remains a reign attestation; Song is the calendar user.

evidence.quote: 道宗清寧十年，宋用《明天曆》；
大安七年，宋用《觀天曆》。

itemChecks.event: Emperor Tianzuo is the explicitly named Liao ruler in Qiantong 6.
itemChecks.reason: Qiantong begins AD 1101, yielding AD 1106 for year 6. The named emperor is contemporary with that reign-year reference; the subsequent verb belongs to Song. No birth, death, day-level conversion or assertion about the whole reign is made.

evidence.quote: 天祚皇帝乾統六年，宋用《紀元曆》。

itemChecks.reason: The two hints reproduce supported AD 956 and 960 attestations. They are not a continuous activity interval and do not transfer the Later Zhou or Song reforms to Muzong.

十年，宋用建隆《應天曆》。

itemChecks.reason: AD 982 matches Qianheng 4 and does not claim survival past his death during that year. The hint carries no calendar-reform authorship.

evidence.quote: 景宗乾亨四年，宋用《乾元曆》。

itemChecks.event: Shengzong's separate Tonghe and Taiping reign references.
itemChecks.reason: AD 1001 and 1021 match the two explicit regnal contexts. These discrete hints do not imply uninterrupted activity or personal adoption of Song calendars.

evidence.quote: 聖宗統和十九年，宋用《儀天曆》；
太平元年，宋用《崇天曆》。

itemChecks.reason: AD 1064, 1075 and 1091 match Qingning 10, Dakang 1 and Da'an 7. The hint array records separate attestations, not a lifespan or an assertion of activity in every intervening year.

大康元年，宋用《奉元曆》；
大安七年，宋用《觀天曆》。

itemChecks.reason: AD 1106 matches Qiantong 6. It is neither a birth/death estimate nor the date of an action performed personally by Tianzuo.

references.reason: Checked Liao era starts: Yingli 951, Qianheng 979, Tonghe 983, Taiping 1021, Qingning 1055, Taikang 1075, Taian 1085, Qiantong 1101. These supply conventional year labels only. The table uses variant spellings and abridged terminal years; its endpoints are not used as personal death dates.

references.title: Chinese historical era table, Liao section
references.reason: The Liao rows corroborate the eight starts, associate them with the correct rulers, and identify Dakang/Taikang and Da'an. Qianheng continues under Shengzong after his accession in 982; a year label alone never identifies who was alive at every point in that year.

Primary annal confirms Jingzong died within Qianheng 4, so AD 982 is a valid year-of-life attestation but not evidence for survival throughout the year. No external birth/death claim is added to chapter 043.
